---
title: "Decisions"
subtitle: "The Decide phase: what was decided, against which rule, on what evidence"
---

Each decision below is checked against a rule that was written in the build plan before this
phase started. The evidence is what the repository and its runs showed on 16 November 2026.
A decision is revisited on the date it gives, or sooner if the evidence changes.

## Backend: stay static

**Rule.** Stay on static files until one of five triggers fires. Each trigger is a need that
precomputed files cannot meet.

| Trigger | Evidence on 16 November 2026 | Fired? |
|---|---|---|
| Users want their own watchlists or alerts | There are no accounts and no requests for them. | No |
| Published data passes about 500 MB, or pages need queries too heavy for a browser | Every published table together is 3.1 MB (`site/data/v1/`), and the largest single table is 1.3 MB. | No |
| A source needs refreshing more often than hourly | The fastest source is collected daily; the rest weekly or monthly. | No |
| Licensed or paid data is added | Bright Data, a paid provider, is set up on its free allowance, and its raw rows are never committed or published. None of today's published tables use it: the price tables list only Central Computers and Blender Open Data as sources. | No, but watched |
| The site starts charging or selling | Nothing is sold. | No |

**Decision: stay static.** Revisit the day any trigger fires, and at the latest at the
six-month review in May 2027. The Bright Data line fires if a paid plan is bought, or if its
listings ever need to be served rather than summarised.

## US Housing: no-go for now

**Rule.** Build US Housing only if modules 1 to 4 are stable.

**Evidence.** They are built, but not yet stable by their own tests:

- Harden: the 30 days with no silent failure started on 15 November, so it cannot finish
  before 15 December.
- Macro Monitor: the full monthly cycle on schedule is still open.
- Federal Procurement: the 1% totals criterion as written is not met (95 of 121 months). The
  row-by-row check explains 25 of the 26 missed months, and one is still to be checked.
- GitHub started the scheduled daily run hours late on both days so far (about six and seven
  hours). On 15 November a run was started by hand before the late one arrived.

**Decision: no-go until the Harden exit is met.** Revisit on 15 December 2026. Even then, US
Housing goes ahead only if no failure Issue has opened in the 30 days before.

## Demand Radar: run the two-week experiment, designed now

**Rule.** Treat the radar as research, not product: a two-week experiment, then a written
go or no-go.

**What is possible.** Three of the four inputs the plan names need something the pipeline does
not have. Google Trends has no API, so it needs a manual export. YouTube metrics need a key.
Marketplace and forum data are ruled out by their terms. Two inputs are free and automatic:
Wikimedia pageviews (daily since July 2015, open licence, no key) and Census monthly retail
sales by kind of business (the Census key is already set up).

**The test, fixed before any data is pulled.** The details were settled on 16 November 2026,
after checking only which categories and articles exist, and before any figure was fetched.
They are in [`pdi/radar/config.py`](https://github.com/liumOazed/public-data-intelligence/blob/main/pdi/radar/config.py).

- Question: does attention to a product category lead US spending on it?
- Attention: monthly pageviews by people (not bots) on English Wikipedia, summed over a fixed
  list of articles for each category. The change is measured on the same month a year earlier.
- Spending: Census monthly retail sales (MARTS, not seasonally adjusted) for the matching kind
  of business, also as the change on the same month a year earlier. Comparing with a year
  earlier removes the seasons from both series in the same way.
- Pairs, four tests:

  | Census kind of business | Articles |
  |---|---|
  | 443 Electronics and appliance stores | Laptop, Television, Smartphone, Video game console, Headphones, Refrigerator, Washing machine |
  | 442 Furniture and home furnishings stores | Furniture, Couch, Mattress, Bed, Table (furniture) |
  | 448 Clothing and clothing accessories stores | Clothing, Jeans, Dress, Sneakers, Coat (clothing) |
  | 451 Sporting goods, hobby, musical instrument and book stores | Bicycle, Golf, Camping, Fishing tackle, Guitar, Book, Board game, Jigsaw puzzle, Treadmill |

- Baseline: persistence, meaning last month's change in sales.
- Model: the baseline plus last month's change in pageviews, one straight line.
- Pass: the model beats the baseline on months it never saw, by more than twice the standard
  error of the gain in absolute error. This is the same bar as the Trade lead-time test. Fit
  on months up to December 2021, score once on January 2022 onwards.
- Every result is logged, and a pass is a prediction for that pair only. Four tests at this bar
  can produce a false pass by chance, so a single pass is reported with that caveat.

**Decision: go for the experiment.** Two weeks from 16 November, written up by 30 November
2026. Whether the radar becomes a module is decided then, on that result.

## Lead-lag studies: a plan for May 2027

**Rule.** Plan lead-lag studies only for series with six months or more of our own history.
A lead found in the past is not proof of cause.

**Evidence.** The pipeline began keeping its own first-published values on 15 November 2026:
23,325 macro values, plus the energy figures. Six months of that history arrive on 15 May
2027. The Trade lead-time test of 15 November used latest values and found no signal.

**Plan, fixed now.** Six tests, run once from 15 May 2027 on first-published values only:

1. US imports from Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia leading each economy's own reported exports
   (IMF). This repeats the Trade test in real time. Three tests.
2. Indeed's US job postings index leading the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls. One test.
3. Electricity demand per day leading industrial production in the United States and
   Malaysia. Two tests.

Each test uses the Trade lead-time rule: a persistence baseline, a gain of more than twice its
standard error out of sample, and the result published either way. A pass is labelled a
prediction for that pair only and never described as a cause. All six go in the failures log,
passes and failures alike.
